channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek MP Notes Increased Critical Analysis and Bold Judgments in Media
item.description: Odiljon Tojiyev, a member of the Legislative Chamber and head of the National Association of Mass Media, observes a rise in bold opinions, critical perspectives, and deep analysis within Uzbekistan's media landscape. He emphasizes journalism's role in public control and addressing citizen needs.

item.title: Uzbekistan's SCO Initiatives in Bishkek Lay Foundation for Eurasian Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan presented initiatives at the SCO summit in Bishkek, proposing the 'SCO-2040: Space of Common Development' concept. This strategy shifts the SCO's focus from security to development, aiming to create a platform for investment, technology, and infrastructure projects across Eurasia.

item.title: Uzbekistan and UNICEF to Enhance Social Protection Mechanisms Against Risks
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Economy and Finance met with UNICEF to develop an adaptive social protection strategy. This strategy will improve citizen support measures considering climate, natural, and economic risks, strengthening household resilience and expanding access to social assistance.

item.title: Tajikistan's Migration Agency Invites Citizens to Work in Japan with Salaries Above $2,800
item.description: Tajikistan's Agency for Work and Migration Abroad has announced job opportunities in Japan for Tajik citizens. The agency reported that potential earnings for these positions exceed $2,800 per month, encouraging job seekers to apply.

item.title: New Seven-Story Complex for 'Kyzmat' State Institution Under Construction Near Bishkek Arena
item.description: A new seven-story complex for the state institution 'Kyzmat' is being built near 'Bishkek Arena' and is expected to open in a few months. The facility will house public service centers, staff offices, and a multi-level parking lot.

item.title: Opposition Figure Tilekmat Kurenov Denies Inciting Power Seizure
item.description: Opposition figure Tilekmat Kurenov stated he did not call for a seizure of power after his court hearing was postponed. The session was rescheduled to September 11 due to the absence of his lawyer.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes 'SCO-2040' development concept at Bishkek summit
item.description: At the SCO summit in Bishkek, Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented several initiatives, including a proposal for the 'SCO-2040: Space of Common Development' concept. The plan aims to define a long-term development model for the organization. Leaders from ten member states attended the meeting.

item.title: Uzbekistan's evolving view of Central Asia in its foreign policy discourse
item.description: Uzbekistan has shifted its perspective on Central Asia multiple times over 35 years, exploring integration and later including Afghanistan. The current foreign policy concept, from 2012, prioritizes the region but lacks a clear definition, leading to debates about expanding regional dialogue formats.

item.title: New facilities opened in Panj district, Tajikistan, ahead of Independence Day
item.description: Several new facilities, including an additional school building and a teahouse, were opened in Tajikistan's Panj district on September 3, 2026, coinciding with the 35th anniversary of the country's independence. The school expansion will accommodate 200 students, and the teahouse will create 12 jobs.

item.title: Joint Venture to Oversee Construction of Nuclear Power Plant in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish a joint venture to manage the construction of its first integrated nuclear power plant in the Jizzakh region. The project aims to employ over 10,000 workers, with 65-70% being local personnel. Construction of the first power unit's foundation is underway, with significant concrete poured.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Discusses Fuel and Lubricant Supply Stability
item.description: A meeting chaired by Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Erlist Akunbekov addressed the supply of fuel and lubricants to Kyrgyzstan. Representatives from the Ministry of Energy, ABank, and petroleum product suppliers discussed market conditions and measures for stable supply. Instructions were given to relevant state agencies.

item.title: Young parliamentarians convene for global conference in Samarkand
item.description: The 12th Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians, organized by the Senate of the Oliy Majlis and the Inter-Parliamentary Union, has begun in Samarkand. The forum, themed 'Towards restoring human rights, justice, and human dignity in challenging times,' gathers around 250 delegates from 58 countries and 11 international organizations.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes law to dismiss police inspectors if over 50% of residents express distrust
item.description: A draft law in Uzbekistan aims to establish the status, duties, and social protections for preventive police inspectors. Introduced by the President, the bill passed its first reading in the Legislative Chamber. It proposes dismissing inspectors if more than 50% of residents in their district express distrust.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's fuel and lubricant supply discussed by cabinet
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's cabinet held a meeting to discuss the supply of fuel and lubricants to the country's population and economy. Participants reviewed the current market situation and stable supply issues. No forecasts for fuel price increases were provided, with officials stating it depends on the market.

item.title: Tajikistan and LS Group to Expand Cooperation in Mining and Metallurgy
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Industry met with representatives from South Korea's LS Group to discuss industrial development and future cooperation. Key areas of discussion included the mining and metallurgical sectors, efficient use of mineral resources, and the implementation of modern technologies. They also explored opportunities in critical mineral processing and energy infrastructure projects.

item.title: South Korea E-9 Visa Holders No Longer Need Migration Agency Approval for Job Changes
item.description: Uzbekistan citizens working in South Korea on an E-9 visa no longer require approval from the Migration Agency to change employers. Certain clauses of the tripartite agreement for temporary labor activities have been revised, simplifying the process for migrant workers.

item.title: Uzbekistan sees over 33,000 property and vehicle deals via escrow accounts in August
item.description: Uzbekistan recorded over 33,000 real estate and vehicle transactions using escrow accounts in August. This mechanism ensures secure and transparent settlements, protecting both buyers and sellers. Tashkent led with 10,487 deals, accounting for 31.4% of the total, indicating continued economic activity in these markets.

item.title: Uzbekistan implements new strategy to combat poverty and boost incomes
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched a new strategy to reduce poverty and increase incomes, following a presidential meeting. The poverty rate has decreased from 5.8% to a lower level, benefiting 1.5 million people. While some regions show significant progress, others require further attention to achieve expected results.

item.title: CIS Countries Agree to Strengthen Coordination within UNESCO
item.description: Representatives from Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan met in Minsk to enhance cooperation within UNESCO. Discussions focused on coordinating activities, strengthening inter-commission contacts, and preserving the non-political nature of UNESCO's work.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Transport Ministry faces shortage of qualified personnel
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Transport and Communications is seeking to address a shortage of qualified personnel by strengthening cooperation with universities. The ministry needs specialists in road and rail transport, infrastructure, management, and safety, as demand grows with infrastructure development and technological advancements.

item.title: Azerbaijan-Kyrgyzstan Development Fund capital increased to $200 million
item.description: The capital of the Azerbaijan-Kyrgyzstan Development Fund (AKDF) has been increased to $200 million. The decision was formalized through a second supplementary agreement signed during the Azerbaijani president's state visit to Kyrgyzstan. The fund was initially established in autumn 2022 with $100 million.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes unified energy audit procedure for organizations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's cabinet of ministers has proposed a unified procedure for energy audits of organizations and enterprises. The goal is to establish a single mechanism for energy audits in line with the Law 'On Energy Saving'. The project aims to identify energy saving potential and improve efficiency.

item.title: Syria Begins Destroying Chemical Weapons from Bashar al-Assad Era with UN Support
item.description: Syria has started destroying chemical weapons remaining from the Bashar al-Assad era, with the UN supporting the operation. Toxic substances and production facilities found in May are being eliminated. A Syrian official stated that Israel is hindering the country's efforts to fulfill its international obligations.

item.title: New Public Council Established at Kyrgyzstan's Ombudsman Institute to Enhance Rights Protection
item.description: A new Public Council has been formed at the Institute of the Ombudsman of Kyrgyzstan to provide objective reviews on human rights issues. The advisory body includes experts who will focus on implementing UN recommendations, protecting personal data, and safeguarding environmental rights. Their recommendations will inform the Ombudsman's appeals to government agencies.

item.title: Tajikistan National Bank and UNICEF to Expand Cooperation on Youth Financial Literacy
item.description: The National Bank of Tajikistan and UNICEF discussed strengthening cooperation in developing economic and financial skills for adolescents and youth, including those with disabilities. The meeting focused on implementing a financial literacy program for 2026-2030 and expanding entrepreneurial opportunities for young people.

item.title: Brazilian Guest Praises Kyrgyzstan's Accessibility at World Nomad Games
item.description: A Brazilian guest, Juliana, who uses a wheelchair, praised the accessibility of the 6th World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan. She highlighted the organized assistance, special transport, and the efforts of the Ministry of Labor, allowing people with disabilities to participate fully.

item.title: UN Warns World Approaching Dangerous Global Warming Limit
item.description: The UN Environment Programme warns humanity can still avoid climate catastrophe with immediate action. A new report highlights record heatwaves and floods as evidence of rising global temperatures nearing dangerous limits. UN Secretary-General António Guterres stressed the fight for 1.5 degrees Celsius is a fight for humanity.

item.title: Tajikistan Discusses New Climate Commitments Program in Dushanbe
item.description: Dushanbe hosted a roundtable to present and discuss Tajikistan's new Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0) program. The initiative aims to translate climate commitments into concrete actions in energy, water, agriculture, transport, and infrastructure. It also focuses on enhancing the country's resilience to climate risks like glacier melt and floods.

item.title: Uzbekistan's gas and oil extraction decreased, electricity and gasoline production increased
item.description: In Uzbekistan, the extraction of natural gas, oil, and gas condensate continued to decline in January-July. However, gas production significantly recovered in July after a sharp drop the previous month. Gas condensate production also surpassed last year's levels for the first time this year, according to the National Statistics Committee.

item.title: CSTO ready for joint exercises in 2026, announces General Colonel Andrey Serdyukov
item.description: The Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) is preparing for joint exercises in 2026. General Colonel Andrey Serdyukov briefed representatives from Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, and Tajikistan on the upcoming drills. Key events include the 'Vzaimodeystvie-2026' exercise for rapid reaction forces and 'Rubezh-2026' for Central Asian regional forces.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Congratulates Giorgia Meloni on Longest Tenure as Italian Prime Minister
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev sent a letter to Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, congratulating her on becoming the longest-serving head of government in Italy's history. Mirziyoyev acknowledged her efforts in protecting national interests and enhancing Italy's influence in the EU and globally.

item.title: Construction Completed on New 481.5-Meter Bridge Over Norin River
item.description: The construction of a new 481.5-meter bridge over the Norin River in the Namangan region has been completed. The bridge connects Uychi, Uchqo‘rg‘on, and Norin districts to the regional center. This structure is one of the largest built over a river in Uzbekistan since independence.

item.title: Car Accident in Dangara District Results in Pedestrian Fatality
item.description: A fatal road accident occurred on September 2, 2026, in the Dangara district, according to the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Tajikistan. A Shacman truck struck and killed a pedestrian, Ashurov Mahmadsaid Saidkulovich, while traveling from Bokhtar to Kulyab.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 71.9 Billion Soums of Gas and Electricity Stolen in August
item.description: Uzbekistan's "Uzenergoinspeksiya" identified 321 cases of illegal energy resource use in August, resulting in the theft of 71.9 billion Uzbek soums worth of gas and electricity. Investigations into these incidents are ongoing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Mandates Liability Insurance for Tour Operators
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has approved new rules requiring tour operators to provide tourists with medical or accident insurance. Liability limits will vary based on route difficulty, with costs estimated at 400-500 soms per tourist per day. The government expects this to increase tour package costs by only 1-2 percent.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Social Workers Assist Over 40 People with Disabilities at World Nomad Games
item.description: Approximately 100 social workers from Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Labor are assisting over 40 people with disabilities at the VI World Nomad Games. Special transport is provided for wheelchair users, facilitating their access to events. Both Kyrgyz citizens and foreign visitors have expressed gratitude for the support and inclusive environment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Selling Official Cars Directly to Civil Servants
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a proposal to allow government agencies to sell official vehicles directly to their employees before an auction. The car would be offered to the employee first in line for purchase at market value. If declined, it would proceed to an electronic auction.

item.title: Tajikistan aims to achieve 'A' status for its Ombudsman
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Human Rights Ombudsman met with a UN regional advisor to discuss the institution's development and cooperation in human rights. The Ombudsman's office, currently holding 'B' status since 2012, aims to achieve 'A' status, signifying full compliance with international standards.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan approves concept for science development until 2040
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan has approved a concept for the development of science until 2040. This document outlines long-term directions for state policy in science, aiming to foster research, higher education, intellectual property, and innovation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to revise approach to international organization participation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers approved a new procedure for government agencies' cooperation with international organizations. Specific bodies will be assigned to manage relations, coordinate positions, and represent the country, improving cooperation effectiveness and responsibility distribution.
